cards.explanation: The answer is that David blesses the people in the name of the LORD. When he finishes sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blesses the people in the name of the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:2). The offerings wrap up and good words go out over the people. I'd take a blessing over a plain old handshake any day.

The answer is False. David gave a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake to every man and woman of Israel (1 Chronicles 16:3). The list wasn't just the Levites. That's how you throw a celebration, friends.

The word is thanks. The Levites are appointed to celebrate, to give thanks and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel (1 Chronicles 16:4). All three jobs are pointed at the LORD. I'd take that job without even asking about the pay.

The answer is True. The song says, “let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.” (1 Chronicles 16:10) It's the hearts of the seekers that get the call to rejoice. That's a song worth singing along to, friends.

The song calls the offspring of Israel. It says, “O offspring of His servant Israel, O sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.” (1 Chronicles 16:13) Three ways of saying it, and every one points to the same family. When a call is said three times, you can bet it matters.
The answer is False. The song says, “He is the LORD our God; His judgments carry throughout the earth.” (1 Chronicles 16:14) The song doesn't stop at Israel's border. It says the whole earth.

What God says He will give is the land of Canaan. In the song, God says to Jacob and Israel, ‘I will give you the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance.’ (1 Chronicles 16:18) It's a promise made as an inheritance. Notice it's land, not a thing you can put in your pocket.

The LORD lets no one oppress them. The song says, “He let no man oppress them…” (1 Chronicles 16:21) They were wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another (1 Chronicles 16:20). Wandering is hard enough, but they weren't wandering unwatched.

The word is kings. The song says of the LORD, “He rebuked kings on their behalf…” (1 Chronicles 16:21). Then the LORD says, ‘Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!’ (1 Chronicles 16:22) Even kings got told to keep their hands to themselves.

The reason the song gives is that other gods are idols but He made the heavens. “For all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens.” (1 Chronicles 16:26) On one side, idols. On the other, the One who made the heavens. That's a big gap, friends.

The answer is False. The song says, “Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.” (1 Chronicles 16:28) The families of the nations are called too. That's a big crowd, friends.
The song tells them to bring an offering. It says, “bring an offering and come before Him.” (1 Chronicles 16:29) Nobody's told to show up empty-handed. It's a come-and-bring kind of invitation.

The reason the song gives is that He is coming to judge the earth. “Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for He is coming to judge the earth.” (1 Chronicles 16:33) The reason given is His coming, friends. That's why even the trees sing.

The answer is True. The song says, “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” (1 Chronicles 16:34) Earlier the song just said to give thanks (1 Chronicles 16:8). This time it comes with the reason.

The cry gives this reason: so they may give thanks to His holy name. It says, “…that we may give thanks to Your holy name, that we may glory in Your praise.” (1 Chronicles 16:35) The song ends up right back at thanks. It started there too.
The answer is True. The song ends, and then all the people said, “Amen!” and “…praise the LORD…” (1 Chronicles 16:36) The whole crowd answers back. That's a good way to close a song, friends.

The word is bless. The people head to their homes, and David returns home to bless his household (1 Chronicles 16:43). He blessed the people at the start (1 Chronicles 16:2), and now he blesses his own household. I like a day that opens and closes with a blessing.
